cold_email.subject: Interest in Educator (Seasonal)/ Garden State Plaza — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educator (Seasonal)/ Garden State Plaza opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Administrative Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Touro University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Assistant opportunity with Touro University at Touro University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Patient Service Representative- Temporary Full-Time — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Putnam County Hospital - Greencastle, Indiana Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Patient Service Representative- Temporary Full-Time opportunity with Putnam County Hospital - Greencastle, Indiana at Putnam County Hospital - Greencastle, Indiana.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Dose Formulation Research Technician (3rd Shift) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Labcorp Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Dose Formulation Research Technician (3rd Shift) opportunity with Labcorp at Labcorp.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Urgently Hiring: Administrative Assistant - Cedar Park — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Huntington Learning Center Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Urgently Hiring: Administrative Assistant - Cedar Park opportunity with Huntington Learning Center at Huntington Learning Center.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Engineering Leadership Development Program — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Blue Ventis Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Engineering Leadership Development Program opportunity with Blue Ventis at Blue Ventis.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in AppliedKids Infant-Toddler Teacher (12ECE Units & 3 Infant-Toddler Units) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Applied Medical Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the AppliedKids Infant-Toddler Teacher (12ECE Units & 3 Infant-Toddler Units) opportunity with Applied Medical at Applied Medical.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Dean's Administrative Assistant, College of Arts & Sciences — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Quinnipiac University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Dean's Administrative Assistant, College of Arts & Sciences opportunity with Quinnipiac University at Quinnipiac University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Communications Specialist Job Posting — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Orion Policy Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Communications Specialist Job Posting opportunity with Orion Policy Institute at Orion Policy Institute.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Professional Aide — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Michigan State University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Professional Aide opportunity with Michigan State University at Michigan State University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Administrative Secretary — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Loma Linda University Health Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Secretary opportunity with Loma Linda University Health at Loma Linda University Health.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Program Assistant-Youth ACT — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Greater Mental Health of New York Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Program Assistant-Youth ACT opportunity with Greater Mental Health of New York at Greater Mental Health of New York.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.body:
Dear American University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Program Coordinator, AU Abroad opportunity with American University at American University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role Glean Technologies, Inc. seeks Software Engineer in Mountain View, CA: Job Duties: Develop a software-based platform that can scale indefinitely, including scalable enterprise search solutions. Build large scale fault tolerant distributed systems, preferably with knowledge of performance benchmarking tools and performance tuning on Linux based systems. Perform thorough code review for peers including interface design, code quality and testing strategies. Understand customer requirements and implement them in our solution. Work closely with the company's product teams to understand customer requirements and ensure these features satisfy their requirements and are delivered effectively with high quality. Implement data ingestion pipelines to retrieve data from all enterprise data sources and build a secure search index over all of that data using C++/Java/Python/Go. Design and implement user interfaces used by enterprise workers to search enterprise content and design an API to build other search-based applications. Telecommuting permitted. Minimum Requirements: Master’s degree, or foreign equivalent, in Computer Science, Engineering (any), Information Technology, or closely related quantitative discipline and two (2) years of experience in job offered or two (2) years of experience in the field of software development, data science, or related occupation Special Skills: Machine Learning/Deep Learning Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) Python PyTorch TensorFlow Anomaly Detection Scikit-learn AWS NLP Security and data engineering Any suitable combination of education, training and experience is acceptable. Location: Mountain View, CA. Telecommuting is an option. Compensation & Benefits The standard base salary range for this position is $215,000 - $278,900 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. Submit a resume with references using the apply button on this posting or by email at: jobs@glean.com at Req.# L24-158959. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. Global Data Privacy Notice for Job Candidates and Applicants: Depending on your location, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), or other privacy laws may regulate the way we manage the data of job applicants. Our full notice outlining how data will be processed as part of the application procedure for applicable locations is available in our Privacy Policy . By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. US applicants and their applications are subject to arbitration of disputes as outlined in our Applicant Arbitration Agreement . By clicking “Submit Application,” I confirm that I have read the Global Data Privacy Notice and the Applicant Arbitration Agreement , and I agree to the terms.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Child Care Assistant INT 6854 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Coast Guard Exchange (USCGCSC) Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Child Care Assistant INT 6854 opportunity with Coast Guard Exchange (USCGCSC) at Coast Guard Exchange (USCGCSC).

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role Glean Technologies, Inc. seeks Software Engineer in Mountain View, CA: Job Duties: Develop a software-based platform that can scale indefinitely, including scalable enterprise search solutions. Build large scale fault tolerant distributed systems, preferably with knowledge of performance benchmarking tools and performance tuning on Linux based systems. Perform thorough code review for peers including interface design, code quality and testing strategies. Understand customer requirements and implement them in our solution. Work closely with the company's product teams to understand customer requirements and ensure these features satisfy their requirements and are delivered effectively with high quality. Implement data ingestion pipelines to retrieve data from all enterprise data sources and build a secure search index over all of that data using C++/Java/Python/Go. Design and implement user interfaces used by enterprise workers to search enterprise content and design an API to build other search-based applications. Minimum Requirements: Master’s degree, or foreign equivalent, in Computer Science, Engineering (any), Information Technology, or closely related quantitative discipline Special Skills: C++ Java Python Go JavaScript Distributed Systems Machine Learning PyTorch Ci/CD Pipelines GCP Any suitable combination of education, training and experience is acceptable. Experience can be gained through coursework, scholastic achievement, or work experience. Location: Mountain View, CA. Telecommuting permitted. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. Submit a resume with references using the apply button on this posting or by email at: jobs@glean.com at Req.# L25-163426. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. jobs.title: Electrical Engineer
jobs.description: Use Your Power for Purpose At Pfizer, we believe that every role contributes to our mission of improving patients' lives. Whether you are involved in the design and development of manufacturing processes or supporting the upkeep of critical systems, engineering is crucial to ensuring customers and patients receive the medicines they need. By collaborating with our forward-thinking engineering team, you will help accelerate the delivery of medicines to the world. What You Will Achieve In this role, you will: • Support the operation, maintenance, reliability, and lifecycle management of site electrical utility, power distribution, and emergency power systems, including substations, transformers, switchgear, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, and emergency generators. • Support electrical capital and infrastructure projects through design reviews, field investigations, construction support, commissioning, and project closeout activities. • Provide engineering support for the development of scopes of work, project execution plans, and engineering studies for equipment installation or modification. • Provide field engineering support during maintenance, troubleshooting, commissioning, outages, and capital project execution activities. • Maintain and update electrical one-line diagrams, equipment databases, panel schedules, power monitoring systems, maintenance plans, and other engineering documentation. • Ensure engineering and maintenance activities are performed in accordance with Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), applicable standard operating procedures (SOPs), quality requirements, electrical safety standards, and regulatory requirements. • Assist with electrical engineering studies, including load flow, short-circuit, voltage drop, protective device coordination, and arc-flash analyses. • Support electrical asset condition assessments, preventive maintenance optimization, equipment criticality reviews, and obsolescence planning activities. • Participate in Root Cause Failure Analysis investigations and update equipment reliability plans in collaboration with Production and Quality team leads. • Promote workplace safety by following site safety procedures and performing proactive safety assessments. • Actively participate in site and corporate initiatives. Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements) • Applicant must have a bachelor's degree with at least 2 years of experience; OR a master's degree with 0+ years of experience; OR an associate's degree with 6 years of experience; OR a high school diploma (or equivalent) and 8 years of relevant experience • Knowledge of or experience with medium-voltage electrical distribution systems, including design, operation, maintenance, or project support. • Working knowledge of applicable electrical codes and safety standards, including NFPA 70, NFPA 70E, and relevant OSHA electrical safety requirements. • Experience with Root Cause Failure Analysis, Equipment Criticality Ranking, preventive and predictive maintenance optimization, and/or Failure Modes and Effects Analysis. • Working knowledge and understanding of Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and applicable GxP requirements. • Ability to read and interpret electrical one-line diagrams, equipment drawings, technical specifications, and manufacturer documentation. • Excellent oral and written communication skills. • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications. • Ability to analyze technical issues, communicate recommendations clearly, collaborate across functional teams, and seek guidance when appropriate. Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements) • Experience in the pharmaceutical sector. • Proficiency in technical writing and document review. • Knowledge of industrial utility systems, electrical reliability practices, power monitoring technologies, or electrical asset management principles. • A proactive approach to promoting workplace safety. • Experience using common artificial intelligence tools, including generative technologies such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot, to support problem-solving and enhance productivity; curiosity about how these tools can improve outcomes; and an understanding of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use. Additional Information • Relocation support may be available. • Work location assignment: On Premise. The annual base salary for this position ranges from $82,700.00 to $137,900.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 10.0% of the base salary. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility. Candidates must be authorized to be employed in the U.S. by any employer. U.S. work visa sponsorship (such as TN, O-1, H-1B, etc.) is not available for this role now or in the future. Sunshine Act Pfizer reports payments and other transfers of value to health care providers as required by federal and state transparency laws and implementing regulations. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. Therefore, if you are a licensed physician who incurs recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Pfizer that we pay or reimburse, your name, address and the amount of payments made currently will be reported to the government. If you have questions regarding this matter, please do not hesitate to contact your Talent Acquisition representative. EEO & Employment Eligibility Pfizer is committed to equal opportunity in the terms and conditions of employment for all employees and job applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability or veteran status. Pfizer also complies with all applicable national, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act and IRCA. Pfizer is an E-Verify employer. This position requires permanent work authorization in the United States. Pfizer endeavors to make www.pfizer.com/careers accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding the accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process and/or interviewing, please email disabilityrecruitment@pfizer.com . This is to be used solely for accommodation requests with respect to the accessibility of our website, online application process and/or interviewing. jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role Glean Technologies, Inc. seeks Software Engineer in Mountain View, CA: Job Duties: Design, develop, and maintain full-stack applications spanning front-end interfaces, REST APIs, and application servers. Build and optimize user-facing features using TypeScript and React. Develop server-side services and tooling using Node.js and Flask. Write and maintain backend systems and services in Java and C++. Perform data analytics and data visualization to inform product decisions and system performance. Apply algorithm design skills to solve complex engineering problems across distributed systems. Minimum Requirements: Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Engineering, or a closely related field. Any suitable combination of education, training and experience is acceptable. Special Skill Requirements: Full-stack development TypeScript React Data analytics and data visualization Node.js Flask Java C++ Algorithm design Special skills can be gained through academic coursework, scholastic achievement, or professional experience. Location: Mountain View, CA. Partial telecommuting permitted from within a commutable distance. Compensation & Benefits The standard base salary range for this position is $187,075 - $234,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. Submit a resume with references using the apply button on this posting or by email at: jobs@glean.com at Req.# L25-161399. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. Global Data Privacy Notice for Job Candidates and Applicants: Depending on your location, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), or other privacy laws may regulate the way we manage the data of job applicants. Our full notice outlining how data will be processed as part of the application procedure for applicable locations is available in our Privacy Policy . By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. US applicants and their applications are subject to arbitration of disputes as outlined in our Applicant Arbitration Agreement . jobs.description: MongoDB’s Incident & Escalation Management (IEM) function coordinates cross-functional responses to critical customer situations and drives improvements to how we respond over time. We’re looking for a Senior Program Manager to strengthen the function’s ability to deliver its program priorities consistently across regions through focused planning, disciplined execution, clear visibility, and dependable follow-through. As an execution partner to IEM leadership, you’ll help turn strategic priorities and operational learnings into a measurable book of work. You’ll establish clear plans, ownership, operating cadences, risk visibility, and follow-through, while bringing an informed external perspective on relevant industry practices. You’ll partner with the IEM team and stakeholders across Technical Services, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, Sales, and other teams in the Americas, Asia Pacific, and EMEA. This is a program-management role - not an incident commander or technical investigator role. Functional leaders and incident responders retain accountability for strategy, policy, technical decisions, people leadership, and live operational response. You’ll own the execution system around prioritized work so leaders and subject-matter experts can focus on customers, technical judgment, incident leadership, and their teams. We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Dublin for our hybrid working model. What you’ll do Own the IEM program of work and its supporting materials, maintaining a clear roadmap of outcomes, priorities, owners, milestones, dependencies, capacity considerations, commitments, and decisions Partner with IEM leaders and sponsors to identify and prioritize strategic focus areas, assess opportunities to mature the function, and recommend practical improvements aligned with relevant industry practices Turn ambiguous needs into scoped, measurable work. Clarify outcomes, sequence milestones, establish accountable owners, document decisions and delivery expectations, and coordinate technical and cross-functional reviews Drive delivery across Technical Services, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, Sales, and partner teams. Clarify accountability and handoffs, resolve dependency gaps, and surface blockers, capacity constraints, and resourcing risks early—with options and recommendations Establish and run planning, program-review, and risk-review cadences. Keep backlogs and program records current and decision-ready, track commitments, facilitate decisions, and follow agreed actions through closure Connect IEM program works with the Customer Organization’s wider PMO, aligning planning, governance, dependencies, and reporting to ensure organizational alignment and visibility Help translate recurring incident and escalation patterns, post-incident findings, customer-impacting gaps, and corrective actions into prioritized improvement work with owners, timelines, milestones, and verifiable closure criteria. Coordinate root-cause analysis completion and customer incident-report delivery with clear ownership and quality expectations Advance incident-response and escalation practices, including frameworks and playbooks, readiness, communications, training, simulation exercises, post-incident review, and consistent implementation across teams and regions Partner with data and tooling teams to improve operational instrumentation, metrics, reporting, workflow integration, and automation. Help ensure AI-enabled workflows are appropriately governed, measured, and human-reviewed. Mature program reporting by refining outcome and health measures, improving data quality and consistency, establishing baselines, and turning operational data into actionable insights - not simply reporting activity or optimizing a single response-time metric Prepare concise updates, requirements, specifications, operating proposals, decision records, and executive-ready summaries that make progress, trade-offs, risks, and decisions clear Coordinate readiness and adoption so approved changes to processes, tooling, roles, communications, and operating procedures are understood, operationalized, and sustained What success looks like Priority initiatives have clear outcomes, accountable owners, realistic milestones, active risk tracking, and reliable follow-through Leaders have an accurate, timely view of program health, delivery risks, dependencies, capacity constraints, and decisions needed Post-incident and post-escalation learning becomes prioritized, durable improvement; corrective actions have clear owners and do not remain open-ended Readiness, handoffs, communications, and closure practices become more consistent and measurable across teams and regions Escalation Managers, Incident Commanders, and technical experts spend less time coordinating program work and more time applying their expertise to customers, incidents, and teams Program measures guide decisions and improvement, while execution reliability and stakeholder confidence increase How success will be assessed The role will be evaluated on program health and operational outcomes - not meeting or status-report volume. Measures will be baselined during the first 60–90 days and refined with leadership. They may include: The share of priority initiatives with clear outcomes, accountable owners, milestones, and active risk tracking Initiatives and process improvements completed and adopted Closure rate and aging of post-incident and post-escalation actions, overdue actions, and unresolved dependencies Evidence that recurring incident and escalation patterns are being addressed through durable process, tooling, or product changes Stakeholder confidence in visibility, coordination, and decision follow-through Sampled estimates of coordination time returned to operational leaders and subject-matter experts What you’ll bring 7–10 years of progressive program or project management experience, with a track record of growing responsibility - from coordinating smaller initiatives to leading complex, cross-functional programs. Experience outside the technology sector is welcome Significant experience leading complex, cross-functional programs in a global enterprise or similarly demanding environment, delivering through a matrix rather than relying on direct authority Demonstrated experience with incident response, major-incident management, customer escalations, crisis management, service operations, trust & safety, or closely related operational programs at scale. You understand the lifecycle from detection and triage through coordination, communication, mitigation, review, and follow-through A track record of building or improving operational programs - not only tracking projects - including governance, operating cadences, roles and handoffs, readiness, metrics, and continuous-improvement mechanisms Strong project and program-management fundamentals, including program prioritization, scope and outcome definition, sequencing, dependency and risk management, capacity awareness, backlog discipline, stakeholder alignment, delivery governance, and change adoption Experience establishing useful operating cadences and decision-ready reporting, and working with operational data to set baselines, interpret trends, and turn evidence into practical recommendations The ability to structure ambiguous requests into clear requirements, operating proposals, decision records, and measurable work. cold_email.subject: Interest in 2027 - Software Engineering Intern, AMER — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear MongoDB Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the 2027 - Software Engineering Intern, AMER opportunity with MongoDB at MongoDB.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: Scientist, IVD BioDevelopment Position Summary Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. We measure tumor-derived cfDNA at the molecular level to help inform personalized health care decisions with a non-invasive test. Natera R&D is seeking a highly motivated Scientist to join the rapidly growing assay development team to help build the future of Natera. In this position, you will work with high-performing cross-functional teams to develop laboratory tests that benefit our patients and the business. The ideal candidate has a deep understanding of molecular biology, strong scientific curiosity, demonstrated experience in developing Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) technologies and proven experience developing and validating assays through the product development cycle. You will plan, execute, and lead scientific studies under design control in a regulated environment, helping to improve and expand Natera’s oncology product portfolio. Primary Responsibilities Leads in-laboratory efforts and performs duties largely independent from manager Plan, execute, analyze, and present data from moderate- to high-complexity experiments, including hands-on troubleshooting and root-cause analysis for development, verification and validation studies. Coordinate study design, sample size justification, acceptance criteria, and analysis with biostatistics and bioinformatics; perform basic data analysis (e.g., Excel, JMP) Characterize analytical performance studies following CLSI guidance Author and review SOPs, protocols, study reports, and transfer documents for production implementation; contribute to design control deliverables (design inputs/outputs, risk assessments per ISO 14971) in line with CLIA, CAP, 21 CFR Part 820/QMSR, and ISO 13485 Communicates progress directly with colleagues and senior management. Provides regular updates, outcomes, risks, and next steps at laboratory and department meetings Documents research progress under an Electronic Quality Management System Train junior team members on new SOPs and laboratory workflows, and provide technical guidance and troubleshooting support to laboratory operations Be flexible to lead multiple studies and laboratory priorities while maintaining targeted timelines; perform other duties as assigned Employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire. We are seeking a dedicated and independent Scientist 3 to lead lab-based translational research and discovery efforts in lung and gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. Key Responsibilities: This is a hands-on, laboratory-based position that offers the chance to collaborate closely with teams across Genentech Research & Early Development (gRED) - including Research Oncology, Computational Sciences, and Translational Genomics and Proteomics. As an integral member of this cross-functional team, you will: Design and execute experiments to validate biological and therapeutic hypotheses derived from non-clinical, clinical, and real-world data Synthesize, analyze, and interpret experimental and computational data in collaboration with experts from other functions Elucidate mechanisms of action and therapeutic resistance to tumor microenvironment and tumor targeted therapies (eg next-generation checkpoint inhibitors and antibody drug conjugates) to guide patient selection, pharmacodynamic biomarker assessment, combination treatment strategies, and next-generation target identification Identify, evaluate, and validate innovative cell-based, biochemical, and multi-omic assays-including single-cell and functional genomics technologies- to enable scalable hypothesis testing Proactively establish new internal and external collaborations to access emerging technologies, datasets, and analytical methods that fuel translational innovation Qualifications Education: Ph.D. degree in Cancer Biology, Cell Biology, Immunology, or related disciplines. An understanding of lung and GI cancer disease biology, tumor–immune interactions, and key oncogenic signaling pathways would be advantageous. Technical proficiency: proven ability to independently lead hands-on, lab-based research and to develop, optimize, and apply fit-for-purpose experimental assays using relevant preclinical models and human samples. Multidisciplinary expertise in complementary approaches such as primary immune and/or tumor cell isolation and culture, immune-cell functional and tumor-killing assays, target-engagement and pharmacodynamic biomarker assays, multiparameter flow cytometry, and 2D/3D tumor microenvironment models, including ex vivo and in vivo approaches where appropriate. About the role As a Communications Manager at Anthropic, you will bring The Anthropic Institute's research to the world. The Institute works to advance the public conversation around AI, publishing findings so that policymakers, researchers, journalists, and the public can reckon with what's here and prepare for what's ahead. You will provide dedicated communications coverage for the Institute's two largest and fastest growing research engines: 1) Economic Research, which tracks AI's effect on jobs, wages, and the broader economy through the Anthropic Economic Index and labor market analysis, and 2) Societal Impacts, which studies how Claude is actually used, from workplace impacts and personal guidance to Claude's values and frontier agent use. You’ll also support TAI’s other teams, including Special Projects and the Frontier Red Team. In this role, you'll drive research tracking, publication strategy, and reactive press across both portfolios, including launches like quarterly Economic Index releases and the rollout of the new Economic Research Fund. You'll partner closely with the Economic Research and Societal Impacts research teams day to day, work alongside the Deputy Communications Lead, and coordinate with Anthropic's broader communications, policy, and editorial teams to keep messaging aligned while maintaining the Institute's distinct voice. planning and launch execution for the Anthropic Economic Index, recurring labor market analyses, and new research initiatives like the Economic Research Fund Develop narratives that translate technical and quantitative research for audiences well beyond specialist communities Build and maintain relationships with reporters across economics, labor, technology, research, and general interest outlets, along with academic economists and think tank researchers Draft communications plans, briefing documents, talking points, press materials, and social content Manage reactive press on sensitive findings in partnership with the Communications Lead, Deputy Communications Lead, and policy team Partner with policy and editorial teams on publishing strategy, ensuring research reaches the largest appropriate audience through the Anthropic blog, the Institute's site, microsites, interactive experiences, video, and audio Present researchers for media interviews, podcast appearances, and speaking engagements, and prepare them to succeed in those moments Partner with Institute communications leadership on major announcements and milestone engagements Build repeatable rollout playbooks and processes that allow a lean team to cover a growing research portfolio Track both teams' research agendas to shape findings early and plan publications months in advance You may be a good fit if you Have deep communications experience, with significant depth in research, science, economics, or policy communications Have a track record of translating complex, technical, or academic research into public narratives that reach audiences well beyond specialist communities Are comfortable reading and interrogating quantitative research, and can engage substantively and credibly with the researchers who produce it Have strong, active media relationships Can move between long-lead strategic messaging and fast-turnaround tactical execution without losing quality, from planning a launch months out to handling an inbound press inquiry the same day Have led multi-channel rollouts spanning strategy, digital, press, and cross-functional approvals Are intellectually curious about AI's impact on the economy, society, and the future of work, and can embrace the unexpected in a field where the unusual is the norm Thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities shift and ambiguity is common Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial Strong candidates may also have Experience at a research institution, think tank, economics publication, or policy organization communicating quantitative findings Familiarity with the AI policy landscape and the debates around AI's labor market and societal impacts Experience standing up communications processes or playbooks on a small, growing team A background working directly with economists, social scientists, or academic researchers on publication strategy Experience managing Dear Conduent Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Training Operations Coordinator opportunity with Conduent at Conduent.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. jobs.description: Supervisor, Prior Authorization Job Summary The Supervisor, Prior Authorization is responsible for overseeing the daily operations and performance of teams supporting the Prior Authorization function within Natera's Billing Operations department. This position provides direct operational oversight of the Prior Authorization Denials & Appeals, PA360, and PA Mismatch teams, including both domestic and offshore employees. The Supervisor is responsible for ensuring timely and accurate resolution of prior authorization issues, managing team productivity and quality, monitoring payer requirements, and driving operational improvements that support authorization compliance and minimize reimbursement delays. This role partners closely with internal stakeholders and external teams to resolve escalated issues, identify process inefficiencies, and optimize prior authorization workflows. Key Responsibilities Oversee the daily operations of the Prior Authorization Denials & Appeals, PA360, and PA Mismatch teams, ensuring efficient workflow management, timely case resolution, and adherence to departmental performance standards. Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and performance management for both domestic and offshore team members, ensuring consistency in processes, quality, and productivity across teams. Monitor team performance against established KPIs, including productivity, turnaround times, case resolution rates, quality, backlog management, and other operational metrics. Oversee the review, investigation, and resolution of prior authorization denials, including coordination of appeals, identification of denial trends, and implementation of corrective actions to reduce recurring issues. Ensure timely identification, investigation, and resolution of prior authorization discrepancies, mismatches, and other authorization-related issues that may impact claim processing or reimbursement. Monitor work queues, case volumes, and aging inventory to ensure appropriate workload distribution, timely follow-up, and resolution of outstanding authorization cases. Serve as an escalation point for complex prior authorization issues, payer disputes, authorization discrepancies, and other operational challenges requiring additional investigation or cross-functional coordination. Collaborate with internal teams, including Billing, Insurance Verification, Denials & Appeals, and other Revenue Cycle functions, to resolve authorization-related issues and improve end-to-end billing workflows. Partner with offshore team leads and operational stakeholders to ensure alignment on workflows, performance expectations, training, quality standards, and escalation procedures. Identify trends and root causes contributing to prior authorization denials, authorization mismatches, processing delays, and other operational inefficiencies; recommend and implement process improvements. Ensure team adherence to payer-specific authorization requirements, internal policies and procedures, documentation standards, and applicable healthcare regulations. Conduct regular quality reviews and audits to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established prior authorization processes and payer guidelines. Prepare, analyze, and communicate operational performance reports, identifying trends, areas of concern, and opportunities to improve team efficiency and authorization outcomes. Support the development, implementation, and maintenance of standardized workflows, training materials, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) across assigned teams. Participate in hiring, onboarding, training, employee development, and performance evaluations to build and maintain a high-performing team. Foster a collaborative, accountable, and continuous-improvement-focused team environment that supports operational excellence and departmental objectives. Qualifications Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. 3+ years of healthcare revenue cycle experience, with demonstrated experience in prior authorization, insurance verification, authorization denials, appeals, or related payer authorization processes. 1+ year of experience in a supervisory, team lead, or comparable leadership role. Strong understanding of prior authorization workflows, payer authorization requirements, denial and appeal processes, and the relationship between authorization activities, claims processing, and reimbursement. Working knowledge of commercial and government payer policies, medical necessity requirements, and healthcare billing practices. Experience monitoring operational KPIs, managing work queues, identifying performance trends, and implementing process improvements. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex issues and develop actionable solutions. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate across departments and provide effective coaching and feedback. Ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and lead teams in a fast-paced, high-volume operational environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience supervising prior authorization teams or related revenue cycle functions in a high-volume healthcare, diagnostic laboratory, or specialty testing environment. Experience overseeing geographically distributed teams, including offshore or outsourced operational teams. Familiarity with prior authorization requirements and payer policies specific to diagnostic testing, molecular diagnostics, or genetic testing. Experience managing prior authorization denials, appeals, authorization discrepancies, or payer-related escalations. Proficiency with revenue cycle management systems, payer portals, reporting tools, and Microsoft Excel. Experience developing and implementing process improvements, standardized workflows, and quality assurance initiatives. Healthcare revenue cycle certification (e.g., CRCS, CRCP) or related professional certification. The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. jobs.description: About the Team As AI becomes capable of doing more useful work, the way people access and pay for it needs to evolve. Our mission is to make powerful AI easier to access, its value easier to understand, and new ways of using it easier to bring to market. We work where product experience, platform architecture, and business strategy meet. A new plan or pricing model can change what customers can accomplish—and requires careful engineering across eligibility, entitlements, usage, and subscriptions. We turn that complexity into capabilities that product teams can build on and experiences that customers can trust. Working with Product, Design, Finance, Financial Engineering, and Data Science, we’re shaping a platform that can evolve alongside our models and products. This is an opportunity to help define a new team’s technical direction and build systems that expand what OpenAI can offer. You’ll help decide what to build, establish the architecture, and carry ideas through to working products—from a customer’s first interaction with a plan to the services that determine what they can access and use. The work spans new pricing and packaging capabilities, plan and usage experiences, and the shared UIs and tools that make launches repeatable. You’ll partner closely with Financial Engineering to connect these capabilities to subscription and billing systems, keeping customer access and state consistent as offerings evolve. You’ll have substantial ownership over technical decisions and delivery in an area where the roadmap is still taking shape. Your impact will show up in the experiences you ship, the engineering work you eliminate from future launches, and the opportunities your systems make possible. In this role, you will: - Define and build shared pricing and packaging capabilities, including plan configuration, eligibility, entitlement integrations, and usage allowances. - Create intuitive plan and usage experiences across the stack, connecting polished interfaces to product APIs and backend services. - Turn new commercial ideas into working prototypes and experiments with Product, Finance, and Data Science, then use what you learn to guide the next iteration. - Design integrations with Financial Engineering that preserve correct access and subscription state through plan changes, migrations, asynchronous updates, and partial failures. - Build reusable components and configuration tools that let teams launch offerings with less custom engineering and fewer dependencies. - Take responsibility for production quality through migration planning, staged rollouts, testing, monitoring, and recovery paths. - Shape the technical roadmap, make clear tradeoffs between immediate launches and shared foundations, and develop other engineers through code and design reviews. Position Summary Empower your career and become a future leader in the biopharmaceutical industry by joining Bristol Myers Squibb’s Global Procurement team through our dynamic Leadership Development Program (LDP). This 2.5-year, full-time rotational experience is designed to cultivate the next generation of procurement leaders and is perfect for graduates passionate about Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Operations Management, or related fields. The BMS Procurement Leadership Development Program provides a transformative opportunity to build your skills, expand your network, and accelerate your growth into a future procurement leader. You’ll contribute directly to the supply chain that delivers innovative medicines to patients worldwide and gain critical knowledge of the biopharma industry—all while collaborating with high-caliber professionals across BMS. You will rotate across critical procurement functions—such as sourcing and contracting; procurement operations, transformation, and communications; and category strategy, business partnership, and supplier management -- working on projects that support our mission to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines. Throughout the program, you’ll participate in an in-depth orientation covering BMS’s structure, products, brands, and Procurement’s key role in supporting enterprise objectives. Successful completion of the program positions individuals for possible career growth and expanded leadership opportunities within the organization. All rotations are based in central New Jersey. If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact and accelerate your professional growth, this is the opportunity for you!
